1.note: So printed (הרשב"ן, checked on the scan). The known Magen Avot is by R. Simeon ben Ẓemaḥ Duran, the Rashbatz (הרשב"ץ), who is named again at the end of the next paragraph; final ץ and ן are easily confused, so read as Rashbatz.

2.note: Literally "on the night of the sixth [day], 4 Tishrei, I prayed". Perhaps a night vigil of prayer (the nights of the Ten Days of Repentance); the sense is not certain.

3.note: ח"י read as Ḥemdat Yamim, the anonymous kabbalistic book on the Sabbath and festivals arranged by chapters (the Ḥida mentions it by name in part 2). Here and in the next paragraph ("מהח"י", "וח"י מחנוכה") the same reading is followed.

4.note: The book Birkat Avraham "of R. A. B." (לרא"ב); author not identified (perhaps R. Abraham b. ...).

5.note: Taken as the name of a text read on Yom Kippur, opening with the words "Ne'dar ba-kodesh" ("glorious in holiness", Exod 15:11); not identified.

6.note: ד"ה not resolved. Perhaps דברי הימים (Chronicles), or a commentary ("dibbur ha-matḥil"); with the Targum and Midrash Rabbah "from Vayetze to the end of Va'era" it seems to be a running companion to the weekly portion.

7.note: The surname is spelled עלמיא (as for Signor Ḥayyim עלמיא in part 10); rendered "Alamia" as there. The Italian form is not known.

8.note: יצי"מ = יציאת מצרים, the Exodus. מ"מ not resolved (perhaps מכל מקום, "at any rate", or a reference to a book); left untranslated.

9.note: So printed; read as the Spanish (Italian Spagnoli) congregation of Ferrara. The form איספאנמי is odd and may be a misreading of איספאנייולי.

10.note: The place name is uncertain: the checked text has מגצו, but on the scan the letter looks like ל (מגלו). Not identified; the book Derekh Yashar printed in 1576 is also not identified.

11.note: Abbreviations not resolved. After "my father and teacher and my mother and teacher" they are probably other dead relatives or a teacher: כ"ב perhaps his late wife ("kevodah ..."), מ"ו perhaps מורי ורבי, "my teacher and master".

12.note: A book Midrash be-Ḥiddush "of the Rav, of blessed memory"; which Rav is meant is not clear.

13.note: So printed (נחכמכמתי, checked on the scan), not a word. Read as לא נתנמנמתי, "I did not doze", from the context (a waking night, as at Shavuot in other years).

14.note: Read as the Idra Rabba and Idra Zuta of the Zohar. Since it follows the minor tractates Kallah and Soferim, it may instead be the tractates Derekh Eretz Rabbah and Zuta (ד"א), misprinted as אד'.

15.note: A chronogram. As printed, the marked words add up to 500 (קדקד 208 + נזיר 267 + אחיו 25), not a year after 5537. The resolutions (to shorten the mission, to settle its accounts, to write to his children) fit 5538 [1777–78], the last year of the mission, which follows 5537 in this list. The Ḥida may have marked single letters that the printer marked as whole words (for example ש of ראש 300 + ל, ק, ד, ק, ד of ולקדקד 238 = 538); the year is therefore probable, not certain.

16.note: לה"ר = לשון הרע, evil speech. כ"ה not resolved; left as initials.

17.note: Punctuation and sense uncertain. Read as a list: study, the "remembrances" (probably the six Scriptural remembrances recited daily), for its own sake and in truth.
